cohort: The study included 100 antenatal women who were second gravida, and whose previous pregnancy resulted in a live birth at term.
finding: Short interpregnancy intervals were significantly associated with increased risks of severe anaemia, preterm deliveries, low birth weight, and NICU admissions, whereas long intervals showed higher rates of overt diabetes mellitus and LSCS.
mod_finding: Most deliveries across all interpregnancy interval groups were vaginal, though 30% of women in the long interpregnancy interval group delivered by LSCS.
